rule: Detect unsaved work without changing Doctrine's state: check getScheduledEntityInsertions()/Deletions() and compare each managed entity's current mapped field values with getOriginalEntityData() yourself, without calling computeChangeSets(). problem: Calling computeChangeSets() on the real unit of work when the switch is refused moves Doctrine's saved snapshot of each dirty or new entity forward to its current values. An earlier field change is then left out of the UPDATE, and a pending insert is written with only the columns changed after the refusal, because prepareInsertData builds the INSERT from getEntityChangeSet().
fix: Detect unsaved work without changing Doctrine's state: check getScheduledEntityInsertions()/Deletions() and compare each managed entity's current mapped field values with getOriginalEntityData() yourself, without calling computeChangeSets(). rule: Also record where the pointer is released (a `pointerup` handler that checks its target is the dialog) and close only when both the press and the release were on the backdrop; add the opposite-direction drag to the e2e test.
problem: A drag that starts on the backdrop and ends inside the dialog box still closes the dialog, because the browser sends that click to the shared parent, which is the <dialog> itself, so `event.target === this.dialogTarget` is true even though the release happened inside the box.
fix: Also record where the pointer is released (a `pointerup` handler that checks its target is the dialog) and close only when both the press and the release were on the backdrop; add the opposite-direction drag to the e2e test.

fix: Add an e2e test that clones an open dialog and an open menu back into the page and checks they come back closed, plus one that focuses a button outside an open menu and checks the menu closes.

rule: Add e2e tests that insert a dialog wrapper whose dialog has the open attribute and a menu whose trigger has aria-expanded=true and whose list has no hidden attribute, let Stimulus connect them, then assert the dialog is hidden and not modal and the menu is closed.

fix: Add e2e tests that insert a dialog wrapper whose dialog has the open attribute and a menu whose trigger has aria-expanded=true and whose list has no hidden attribute, let Stimulus connect them, then assert the dialog is hidden and not modal and the menu is closed.

rule: Assert that the dialog's and the open menu list's bounding boxes sit between x=0 and x=360, and keep the scrollWidth check for the page itself.
problem: The 360 px test checks documentElement.scrollWidth while the dialog is open, but a modal dialog is position: fixed in the top layer, so it never makes the page scroll even when it is wider than the screen.
fix: Assert that the dialog's and the open menu list's bounding boxes sit between x=0 and x=360, and keep the scrollWidth check for the page itself.

rule: Add a test that moves focus out of the open menu without a key press or a click (for example by calling focus() on another button) and asserts the menu closes.

rule: Test what only the controller does: open the dialog, take a Turbo-style snapshot (clone the controller element with the dialog still open, or restore one from the Turbo cache), then check that connect() closes the non-modal dialog and that the page behind it can be clicked.
problem: The new test 'removing the dialog controller while it is open leaves the page usable' would pass even with no controller code, because browsers take a modal dialog out of the top layer (the layer that makes the rest of the page inert) as soon as it is removed from the page.

fix: Get the name from the kernel through ReflectionMethod on getContainerClass (or assert that the file exists again after createClient) so a wrong path fails the test loudly, and keep the delete as the route because App\Kernel is final and APP_BUILD_DIR would need a global $_SERVER change.

rule: Add symfony/http-kernel, symfony/event-dispatcher and symfony/service-contracts to composer.json require at the 8.1.* constraint (or confirm an existing repo-wide pattern and record it as an accepted exception).

fix: Add symfony/http-kernel, symfony/event-dispatcher and symfony/service-contracts to composer.json require at the 8.1.* constraint (or confirm an existing repo-wide pattern and record it as an accepted exception).

fix: Add a unit test that parses monolog.yaml for each env (as ComponentGalleryRouteTest does for routes) and checks the exact list of handlers with their formatter and path, so prod's stream handlers are pinned to JSON on php://stdout and so is the prod console handler.

rule: Add a case where the context holds an exception with no message and check that the record message comes back unchanged and no error is raised.

rule: Add a short ADR that replaces ADR-0027's redaction bullet and test line, and ADR-0029's `org_id` log field, with the allow-list design; give both old ADRs a "Superseded in part by" line and list the new ADR in the ADR README index.

fix: Add a short ADR that replaces ADR-0027's redaction bullet and test line, and ADR-0029's `org_id` log field, with the allow-list design; give both old ADRs a "Superseded in part by" line and list the new ADR in the ADR README index.

rule: Change `org_id` to `organization_id` in operations.md and link to the allow-list in security.md.

rule: Only withhold the message where it appears whole, for example by matching it between the quotes Symfony puts around it, or skip messages shorter than a few characters and drop the whole log message in that case.
problem: strtr swaps every copy of a thrown exception's message anywhere in the log message, so a short message such as "Invalid" or "x" also breaks up unrelated words, for example the exception class name in "Uncaught PHP Exception App\InvalidThing".
fix: Only withhold the message where it appears whole, for example by matching it between the quotes Symfony puts around it, or skip messages shorter than a few characters and drop the whole log message in that case.

rule: Add a data-provider case with an unquoted message exactly 16 characters long, which is replaced in place, and one exactly 15 characters long, which withholds the whole log message.
problem: No test pins the 16-character cut-off: the short-message tests use 7- and 8-character messages and the long one uses about 34 characters, so moving MIN_UNQUOTED_EXCEPTION_MESSAGE_LENGTH or swapping >= for > would leave the suite green.
fix: Add a data-provider case with an unquoted message exactly 16 characters long, which is replaced in place, and one exactly 15 characters long, which withholds the whole log message.

rule: Check `mb_check_encoding($exceptionMessage, 'UTF-8')` before building the pattern and use the `str_contains` fallback straight away when it fails, then add a test with a short exception message that is not valid UTF-8.
problem: When a short exception message is not valid UTF-8, it goes into a `/u` regex pattern, so `preg_match` fails to compile the pattern and raises a PHP warning; the `false` fallback only works quietly when the bad bytes are in the log text, not in the pattern.
fix: Check `mb_check_encoding($exceptionMessage, 'UTF-8')` before building the pattern and use the `str_contains` fallback straight away when it fails, then add a test with a short exception message that is not valid UTF-8.

fix: Set `framework.exceptions` for NotFoundHttpException and MethodNotAllowedHttpException to `log_level: debug` (below the handler's info level), and pin it in MonologConfigTest.

rule: Find the query string only after the user-info part (after the last `@`, or after the host), and split hosts only on `,redis://`, `,rediss://` or `,valkey://`; add one test case with a password that contains `?` and `,`.

rule: Change the comment in both files to say the password must URL-encode a comma as %2C (Messenger splits on every comma), and either refuse a raw comma in the user-info or move that test case to the list of rejected DSNs.
problem: The new split assumes a Valkey password can contain a comma, and the test now treats `redis://user:se,c/r?et@valkey-state:6379` as a good DSN, but Symfony's Redis transport (`Connection::fromDsn`) still splits on every comma and rejects that DSN. ValkeyAnswers uses the same split, so `/health/ready` would say the state Valkey is fine while the workers can't start.
fix: Change the comment in both files to say the password must URL-encode a comma as %2C (Messenger splits on every comma), and either refuse a raw comma in the user-info or move that test case to the list of rejected DSNs.

problem: Prod now writes every `info` record to stdout with no buffer, and Symfony's RouterListener logs `Matched route "{route}".` at info on every request. So each container healthcheck (every 10 s) and each load-balancer probe of `/health/*` adds a log line forever, the same kind of noise the 404/405-to-debug change was meant to keep out.
fix: Leave the `request` channel out of the prod `main` handler, or send it to a handler set to `warning`, and pin that in MonologConfigTest.

rule: Either run the comma rule only on the Messenger DSN, or say in the docblock and operations.md that the cache DSN follows the same %2C rule for consistency, not because the cache would break.
problem: The cache Valkey probe (`cache_valkey`, REDIS_CACHE_DSN) now fails on a raw comma in the password, but only Messenger refuses that; Symfony's RedisAdapter, which the cache uses, reads such a password fine, so the docblock's reason doesn't hold for the cache.

rule: Delete the php-http/discovery block from symfony.lock, keep the allow-plugins entry only if something still needs it, and confirm the lock matches the intent with `composer validate --strict` and a Flex recipe check.

rule: Use a BatchSpanProcessor with a bounded queue and a long schedule delay so spans stay in memory during the request and are only sent by the forceFlush in endAndExport after the response, and update the class docblock to match.
problem: The provider uses SimpleSpanProcessor, which sends each span to the collector over HTTP as soon as that span ends, so any child span started from CurrentSpan::context() (the DB spans planned for the next task) would make a blocking export call during the request, before the response goes out.
fix: Use a BatchSpanProcessor with a bounded queue and a long schedule delay so spans stay in memory during the request and are only sent by the forceFlush in endAndExport after the response, and update the class docblock to match.

rule: Prove the timeout with a Symfony MockHttpClient whose response never arrives (or by asserting the timeout and max_duration options the factory passes to the client), and drop the wall-clock assert from the unit suite.
problem: The unreachable-collector test sends a real export to 127.0.0.1:9, where the connection is refused at once, and then checks the time on the real clock against 1.5 s.
fix: Prove the timeout with a Symfony MockHttpClient whose response never arrives (or by asserting the timeout and max_duration options the factory passes to the client), and drop the wall-clock assert from the unit suite.

rule: Add a CurrentSpanResetTest like RequestIdResetTest (begin a span, call services_resetter->reset(), assert span() and context() are null), and add a WorkerResetTest case showing that after a request that threw, the next request starts a new trace.

fix: Add a CurrentSpanResetTest like RequestIdResetTest (begin a span, call services_resetter->reset(), assert span() and context() are null), and add a WorkerResetTest case showing that after a request that threw, the next request starts a new trace.

problem: aMethodOutsideTheKnownListIsNotCopiedIntoTheSpan and aMarkerInTheQueryStringAHeaderAndTheBodyReachesNoSpan never assert the exact status code after their requests.
fix: Call assertResponseStatusCodeSame with the expected code (200 for the POST probe, 500 for the fail route, and whatever the odd-method request should return) right after each request.

rule: Add a factory test that builds the exporter with http/json and checks it uses the JSON content type, for example by capturing the request on a MockHttpClient.
problem: No test covers the http/json protocol branch; only protobuf is ever built.
fix: Add a factory test that builds the exporter with http/json and checks it uses the JSON content type, for example by capturing the request on a MockHttpClient.

rule: Add a functional case using the existing sub-request probe fixture, and assert the root span keeps the main route, the main status code, and no error.type.
problem: No test shows that a sub-request's response or exception leaves the root span's route, status and error alone.
fix: Add a functional case using the existing sub-request probe fixture, and assert the root span keeps the main route, the main status code, and no error.type.

rule: Add a container test that reads the base factory definition's arguments (or compiles it with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set) and asserts each env name is wired to the right argument.
problem: when@test replaces the whole TracerProviderFactory definition, so no test ever runs the real OTEL_* env wiring that prod uses.
fix: Add a container test that reads the base factory definition's arguments (or compiles it with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set) and asserts each env name is wired to the right argument.

rule: Give the OTel SDK the app's PSR logger through LoggerHolder::set(...), behind a filter that keeps only the exception class, instead of disabling it; or check the bool that the export and forceFlush return and log the class-only warning when it is false. Then remove the catch, or keep it only for errors that really do throw.
problem: When the collector is down, nothing gets logged: the OTLP exporter catches the failure itself and reports it to the OTel logger, and the factory turns that logger off with LoggerHolder::disable(), so the warning in this catch block never runs for a real export failure.
fix: Give the OTel SDK the app's PSR logger through LoggerHolder::set(...), behind a filter that keeps only the exception class, instead of disabling it; or check the bool that the export and forceFlush return and log the class-only warning when it is false. Then remove the catch, or keep it only for errors that really do throw.

rule: Use a BatchSpanProcessor, or a small processor that buffers spans, and call forceFlush once in endAndExport so every span of the request goes out together after the response.
problem: SimpleSpanProcessor sends each span over HTTP, waiting for the reply, the moment the span ends, so any child span started from CurrentSpan::context() will block the request for up to a second while the response is still being built.
fix: Use a BatchSpanProcessor, or a small processor that buffers spans, and call forceFlush once in endAndExport so every span of the request goes out together after the response.

rule: Remove the 'a request that arrives with a sampled parent keeps it' part, since head sampling with no parent from the request is the decided behaviour.
problem: The comment says a request that arrives with a sampled parent keeps it, but startSpan calls setParent(false) and never reads the incoming traceparent header, so every request starts a new trace sampled by the ratio alone.
fix: Remove the 'a request that arrives with a sampled parent keeps it' part, since head sampling with no parent from the request is the decided behaviour.

rule: Keep describeRequest only in endAndExport and remove the two earlier calls.
problem: describeRequest runs in recordResponse, recordFailure and endAndExport, but the request attributes it reads don't change after routing, so the call in endAndExport alone gives the same span.
fix: Keep describeRequest only in endAndExport and remove the two earlier calls.

rule: Use a BatchSpanProcessor with a queue and batch size big enough for one request and a long scheduled delay, keep the forceFlush on kernel.terminate, and fix the EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS comment to describe what is actually capped.
problem: SimpleSpanProcessor sends each span to the endpoint as a blocking HTTP call the moment that span ends, so only the root span (which ends on kernel.terminate) is exported after the response.
fix: Use a BatchSpanProcessor with a queue and batch size big enough for one request and a long scheduled delay, keep the forceFlush on kernel.terminate, and fix the EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS comment to describe what is actually capped.

rule: Only set STATUS_ERROR and error.type when the final status is 5xx, for example by deciding in recordResponse or by skipping HttpExceptionInterface exceptions whose status code is below 500, and add a status check to the 404 test.
problem: recordFailure marks the span as an error on every kernel.exception, including the NotFoundHttpException the router throws for an unknown path and the AccessDeniedException a voter throws.
fix: Only set STATUS_ERROR and error.type when the final status is 5xx, for example by deciding in recordResponse or by skipping HttpExceptionInterface exceptions whose status code is below 500, and add a status check to the 404 test.

rule: Drop the parent clause and say the ratio applies to every request, since every request starts a new trace.
problem: The comment says a request that arrives with a sampled parent keeps that sampling decision, but startSpan calls setParent(false) and never reads an incoming traceparent header, so ParentBased never sees a parent.
fix: Drop the parent clause and say the ratio applies to every request, since every request starts a new trace.

rule: Either reword the docblock to name this one global on purpose, or move the call to a single explicit bootstrap point so the factory has no hidden side effect.
problem: The docblock says the provider is built without any global, but create() calls LoggerHolder::disable(), which changes OpenTelemetry's process-wide static logger as a side effect.
fix: Either reword the docblock to name this one global on purpose, or move the call to a single explicit bootstrap point so the factory has no hidden side effect.

rule: Add symfony/http-client-contracts to composer.json require (matching the installed major), or type the constructor argument against a class from a package already required directly.
problem: The fix imports Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\HttpClientInterface, but composer.json does not list symfony/http-client-contracts; it arrives only as a transitive dependency of symfony/http-client.
fix: Add symfony/http-client-contracts to composer.json require (matching the installed major), or type the constructor argument against a class from a package already required directly.

rule: Add a probe route that returns a plain 500 response, and a RequestSpanTest case asserting STATUS_ERROR, status code 500 and no ERROR_TYPE attribute.
problem: No test covers a controller that returns a 500 response without throwing, which is the path where the span should be marked as an error but get no error.type.
fix: Add a probe route that returns a plain 500 response, and a RequestSpanTest case asserting STATUS_ERROR, status code 500 and no ERROR_TYPE attribute.

rule: Reword it to say the queue holds up to 2048 spans per request and they leave in batches of 512, and that spans past 2048 are dropped.
problem: The comment above MAX_QUEUE_SIZE says one request's spans fit in a single batch, but a batch holds 512 spans and the queue holds 2048, so a request with 513 to 2048 spans goes out as several batches, each its own HTTP call with its own one-second cap.
fix: Reword it to say the queue holds up to 2048 spans per request and they leave in batches of 512, and that spans past 2048 are dropped.

rule: Have startStatementSpan and startTransactionSpan return null unless the active span is recording (for example `true !== $this->currentSpan->span()?->isRecording()`), or keep CurrentSpan empty when the span is not recording, so tracing-off and unsampled requests really pay only one check.
problem: When tracing is off, every request still puts a span in CurrentSpan: TracerProviderFactory returns a NoopTracerProvider for an empty endpoint, and RequestSpanSubscriber still begins a non-recording span from it. Unsampled requests do the same, so context() is never null during a web request, and every statement still runs the SqlKind regex, the getTracer/spanBuilder/setParent/setAttribute chain and a try/finally that builds a throwaway span.
fix: Have startStatementSpan and startTransactionSpan return null unless the active span is recording (for example `true !== $this->currentSpan->span()?->isRecording()`), or keep CurrentSpan empty when the span is not recording, so tracing-off and unsampled requests really pay only one check.

rule: Make the repeats possessive, meaning the engine never backtracks into them, by writing `(?:\s++|--[^\n]*+(?:\n|\z)|\/\*.*?\*\/)*+`, or use plain `\s` in place of `\s+` inside the group, then add a test case with a long whitespace prefix before `(`.
problem: The pattern `(?:\s+|--…|/\*…\*/)*` puts a repeated `\s+` inside a repeated group, so when a statement starts with a long run of whitespace followed by something other than a letter (for example an indented `(SELECT …) UNION …`), the regex engine tries every way of splitting that whitespace before it gives up.
fix: Make the repeats possessive, meaning the engine never backtracks into them, by writing `(?:\s++|--[^\n]*+(?:\n|\z)|\/\*.*?\*\/)*+`, or use plain `\s` in place of `\s+` inside the group, then add a test case with a long whitespace prefix before `(`.

rule: Rename it to something like TracingDbalMiddleware or DatabaseTracingMiddleware (and its Driver, Connection and Statement wrappers to match) so the two middlewares read as a pair.
problem: The DBAL middleware is called plain TracingMiddleware while its Messenger twin in the same folder is TracingMessengerMiddleware, so the name does not say it traces database statements.
fix: Rename it to something like TracingDbalMiddleware or DatabaseTracingMiddleware (and its Driver, Connection and Statement wrappers to match) so the two middlewares read as a pair.

rule: Add a test-only route that runs one query inside the request, and assert the exported names are exactly ['db BEGIN','db SELECT','db COMMIT'], each with the request span as parent.
problem: GET / only sends BEGIN and COMMIT, so no test shows a real query (a SELECT) as a child of an HTTP request span; the query cases only run under a root span the test builds by hand.
fix: Add a test-only route that runs one query inside the request, and assert the exported names are exactly ['db BEGIN','db SELECT','db COMMIT'], each with the request span as parent.

rule: Queue a failing TracedProbeMessage and then a passing one, run runTheWorkerUntilIdle, and assert two process spans with different trace ids, no parent, and status ERROR only on the first.

rule: Make the inner whitespace match possessive (`\s++`) or wrap the whole skip group in an atomic group `(?>...)`, so a failed match costs time in line with the length of the SQL.
problem: The regex `(?:\s+|...)*` puts a repeat inside a repeat, so a statement that starts with a long run of whitespace and then a non-letter such as `(` makes PCRE try every way of splitting that whitespace until it hits the backtrack limit, and that runs on every traced statement.
fix: Make the inner whitespace match possessive (`\s++`) or wrap the whole skip group in an atomic group `(?>...)`, so a failed match costs time in line with the length of the SQL.

fix: Reword both comments to say a request's or a handled message's root span, cleared by RootSpanExporter when that span ends.

rule: Call projectRows()->removeAllOf(...$organizationIds) in removeOrganizationOf as well, the same way removeDemoRows does.

fix: Call projectRows()->removeAllOf(...$organizationIds) in removeOrganizationOf as well, the same way removeDemoRows does.

rule: Return false straight away when `$actor->roles()->isLeadOf($subject)` is false, and only call `stepPolicyOf` for a lead, so most viewers of a team page cost no extra query.

fix: Return false straight away when `$actor->roles()->isLeadOf($subject)` is false, and only call `stepPolicyOf` for a lead, so most viewers of a team page cost no extra query.

rule: Give RemoveStep a ?TeamId (null for a company step) and refuse with UnknownStep unless step->teamId() matches it exactly, so the team the caller voted on is the team whose step gets removed; or expose the step's team through StepQueries so the caller can vote on it.
problem: RemoveStep only checks that the step belongs to the organization, not which team it belongs to, and nothing in Workflow's Api tells the UI a step's team, so the caller cannot ask the voter about the right object.
fix: Give RemoveStep a ?TeamId (null for a company step) and refuse with UnknownStep unless step->teamId() matches it exactly, so the team the caller voted on is the team whose step gets removed; or expose the step's team through StepQueries so the caller can vote on it.

problem: SetRule reads the whole rule set, changes one rule, and then the upsert in DbalRuleSets::save writes all three columns back, so two people changing different rules at the same time can overwrite each other.
fix: Lock the row before reading it (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in forOrganization/forTeam when called from SetRule), or update only the one changed column (UPDATE wf_rule_set SET <column> = ? with the column picked from RULE_CODES), and add a two-connection race test like CreateProjectRaceTest.

rule: Have the save write only the rule that changed (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET <that column> = EXCLUDED.<that column>, with the column picked from RuleSet::RULE_CODES and never from input), or lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before reading it.
problem: SetRule reads the whole rule set, changes one rule in PHP, then DbalRuleSets upserts all three columns from that stale copy, with no row lock or version check.
fix: Have the save write only the rule that changed (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET <that column> = EXCLUDED.<that column>, with the column picked from RuleSet::RULE_CODES and never from input), or lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before reading it.

rule: Take the step id as a string in RemoveStep (and return a string from AddStep), and build the StepId inside the command, the same way StepQueries::groupOf checks its id.
problem: RemoveStep takes Workflow's Domain StepId as its argument, and AddStep returns one, but deptrac.yaml line 302 lets Workflow_UI see only Workflow's Application and Api, not its Domain.
fix: Take the step id as a string in RemoveStep (and return a string from AddStep), and build the StepId inside the command, the same way StepQueries::groupOf checks its id.

rule: Check entityManager->contains() first and throw a LogicException, as DoctrineSteps::save does, so save never turns into an insert.
problem: save() just calls add(), which persists and flushes, so settings that are not managed by the EntityManager get inserted as a second row instead of being refused.
fix: Check entityManager->contains() first and throw a LogicException, as DoctrineSteps::save does, so save never turns into an insert.

rule: For the team pass, switch rules that are on in the organization's current rules (for example reset the organization row to the defaults before the team pass, or switch tester_moves_done and no_self_review to values that differ from the starting rules) so a lost update would show in the asserted team row.
problem: The team half of twoSessionsSwitchingDifferentRulesAtOnceKeepBothChanges cannot fail: by then the organization's rules are already (true, false, false), so both sessions start from rules where no_self_review and review_before_test are already off, and the old full-row upsert would also have stored (true, false, false).
fix: For the team pass, switch rules that are on in the organization's current rules (for example reset the organization row to the defaults before the team pass, or switch tester_moves_done and no_self_review to values that differ from the starting rules) so a lost update would show in the asserted team row.

rule: Build the StepId alone inside the try, then call steps->byId() outside it.

fix: Build the StepId alone inside the try, then call steps->byId() outside it.

rule: Drop the isLeadOfTeam parameter from StepChangeRights and let the voter's early return own the lead check, or go back to passing the real isLeadOf result.

fix: Drop the isLeadOfTeam parameter from StepChangeRights and let the voter's early return own the lead check, or go back to passing the real isLeadOf result.

rule: Run the team pass on starting rules where both switched rules are still on: reset the organization row to RuleSet::defaults() before the team pass, run the team pass first, or have the team pass switch rules that are still on in the organization row.
problem: In the team pass of twoSessionsSwitchingDifferentRulesAtOnceKeepBothChanges, both sessions start from the organization's rules, and the first pass has already set those to (true, false, false). Both switched rules are therefore off before either session writes, so the team row comes out the same even with the old write that replaced the whole row.
fix: Run the team pass on starting rules where both switched rules are still on: reset the organization row to RuleSet::defaults() before the team pass, run the team pass first, or have the team pass switch rules that are still on in the organization row.

rule: Load the project for link and unlink with a row lock (Doctrine `LockMode::PESSIMISTIC_WRITE`, which is `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) through a `Projects::byIdForUpdate`, or add a version column, and add a two-session test like `CreateProjectRaceTest` that tries a concurrent link.
problem: LinkProject and UnlinkProject load the project with a plain `byId` (no row lock) and Doctrine then writes `UPDATE tkt_project SET team_id = ? WHERE organization_id = ? AND id = ?` without checking the old value, so two leads linking the same unlinked project at the same time both see `team_id` null and the second silently overwrites the first.
fix: Load the project for link and unlink with a row lock (Doctrine `LockMode::PESSIMISTIC_WRITE`, which is `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) through a `Projects::byIdForUpdate`, or add a version column, and add a two-session test like `CreateProjectRaceTest` that tries a concurrent link.

problem: LinkProject and UnlinkProject read the project with a plain byId (no row lock), check team_id in PHP, and then write it with an unconditional UPDATE, so two leads or admins linking the same unlinked project at the same moment both pass the 'not linked yet' check and the second silently overwrites the first.

rule: Join `matched` to tkt_ticket under the visibility predicate once, in a second MATERIALIZED CTE that carries step_id and match_position, then have the count and page LATERALs read only that small in-memory set by step_id (or number the rows once with row_number() over (partition by step_id order by match_position)).
problem: In search mode both per-step LATERALs read the whole `matched` set (up to 1,000 ids) and join every one back to tkt_ticket, then filter by step, so each search does about steps x 2 x 1,000 primary-key lookups plus visibility checks. The priority path, by contrast, stops early on an ordered index.
fix: Join `matched` to tkt_ticket under the visibility predicate once, in a second MATERIALIZED CTE that carries step_id and match_position, then have the count and page LATERALs read only that small in-memory set by step_id (or number the rows once with row_number() over (partition by step_id order by match_position)).

fix: Say in the messenger.yaml comment and the phase hand-off notes that every async handler of a TicketEvent must set fromTransport: 'async_notify', and add a test that fails when an event.bus handler of TicketCreated has no fromTransport.

rule: Write the two count rows in a fixed key order, for example sorted by (project_id, team_id, visibility), so every transaction locks them in the same order.
problem: moveTicket always updates the old count row first and the new one second, so two changes at the same time that move tickets in opposite directions (one ticket made team-only while another is opened to everyone in the same project) each lock one row and then wait for the other's, which is a deadlock.
fix: Write the two count rows in a fixed key order, for example sorted by (project_id, team_id, visibility), so every transaction locks them in the same order.

rule: Lock the two count rows in a fixed key order before changing them, for example by running the SUBTRACT and ADD in sorted (project, team, visibility) order or with one SELECT ... ORDER BY ... FOR UPDATE.
problem: A count move locks the old count row first and then the new one, so two changes running at the same time that move tickets in opposite directions between the same two rows (one ticket from 'all' to 'team' while another goes from 'team' to 'all' in the same project) can deadlock, and one of them fails with a 500.
fix: Lock the two count rows in a fixed key order before changing them, for example by running the SUBTRACT and ADD in sorted (project, team, visibility) order or with one SELECT ... ORDER BY ... FOR UPDATE.

fix: Clear the stored reviewer when the assignee changes, or check in reviewerToStore or reviewerOf that the stored reviewer is not the assignee, and note this in the P03.T8 hand-off.

rule: When the assignee changes (or when the stored reviewer is the new assignee), clear the stored reviewer so the next Code review chooses again. Otherwise a stored lead reviewer on a ticket later given to the lead makes NoSelfReview (src/Workflow/Application/Transition/NoSelfReview.php:41) read it as the no-one-else fallback, and the lead approves their own code with no override note. At minimum, write this in the P03.T8 hand-off note.
problem: The reviewer is stored once and kept for good, but it was chosen for the assignee at that moment, and nothing clears it when the assignee changes; Give it to (P03.T8) will add exactly that kind of change.
fix: When the assignee changes (or when the stored reviewer is the new assignee), clear the stored reviewer so the next Code review chooses again. At minimum, write this in the P03.T8 hand-off note.
